## Ingredients

– 2½ to 3 lb. chuck roast  
– 2 to 3 T. Thai red curry paste, plus 1 T. more if needed  
– 2 to 3 cups beef bone broth, plus up to 1 cup more to finish  
– 1 medium yellow onion, sliced  
– 1 whole head garlic, cloves peeled (I used 27 cloves! 4 to 6 work too)  
– 2-inch piece ginger, sliced  
– 1 T. honey  
– 1 can (13.5 oz.) full-fat coconut milk  
– Juice of 1 lime  
  
For Serving:  
– Cooked jasmine rice  
– 2 Persian cucumbers, diced  
– 3 green onions, sliced  
– Cilantro and chili oil, optional  
– Lime wedges

## Directions
 
1. Heat oven to 325°F, rack in the middle.  
2. Add chuck roast, 2-3 T. curry paste, 2-3 cups broth, onion, garlic, ginger, and honey to a Dutch oven. Toss everything, coating beef well with paste, especially on top. Broth should reach about ⅔ up the beef.  
3. Put the LID ON. Bake 3½ to 4 hours until the beef shreds easily. If the top needs more browning, remove lid for the last 10 to 20 min when nearly tender.  
4. Transfer beef to a bowl. Strain the braising juices through a fine-mesh strainer, gently pressing the aromatics. Discard solids and skim excess fat.  
5. Shred beef separately and toss with ¼ to ½ cup concentrated braising juices.  
6. Return remaining juices to Dutch oven. For more curry flavor or color, stir in 1 T. extra paste and simmer 5 min.  
7. Add coconut milk and up to 1 cup more broth if you want it brothier. Warm gently 5 min; turn off heat.  
8. Serve rice and beef in bowls. Ladle curry broth AROUND the beef, then finish with cucumber, green onions, chili oil, and lime juice. (I missed the lime in the video, but highly recommend adding it for the extra acidity!)
